key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost—1.20% below the best TPE result.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce simulation-heavy design effort for integrated energy systems spanning photovoltaics, storage, heating and other technologies, rather than optimizing solar cells themselves.
method: Propose configuration changes using prior simulation results and structured memory.
Evaluate 25-year net present cost with annual simulations covering eight technologies.
Keep successful changes, revert unsuccessful ones through git, and record an auditable decision trace.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case, ten 50-simulation runs per LLM were compared with ten 300-evaluation runs per baseline; median evaluations to within 1% of the best design ranged from 18 for Opus to 27.5 for Haiku.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to one building case, and convergence reliability varied across LLMs, so broader validation is needed.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
